In commit 7e2175ebd695 (""KVM: x86: Fix recording of guest steal time /
preempted status"") I removed the only user of these functions because
it was basically impossible to use them safely.
There are two stages to the GFN->PFN mapping; first through the KVM
memslots to a userspace HVA and then through the page tables to
translate that HVA to an underlying PFN. Invalidations of the former
were being handled correctly
column2: but no attempt was made to use the MMU

column1: notifiers to invalidate the cache when the HVA->GFN mapping changed.
As a prelude to reinventing the gfn_to_pfn_cache with more usable
semantics
column2: rip it out entirely and untangle the implementation of

column1: the unsafe kvm_vcpu_map()/kvm_vcpu_unmap() functions from it.
All current users of kvm_vcpu_map() also look broken right now
will be dealt with separately. They broadly fall into two classes:
* Those which map
column2: access the data and immediately unmap. This is

column1: mostly gratuitous and could just as well use the existing user
HVA
column2: and could probably benefit from a gfn_to_hva_cache as they

column1: do so.
* Those which keep the mapping around for a longer time
even using the PFN directly from the guest. These will need to
be converted to the new gfn_to_pfn_cache and then kvm_vcpu_map()
can be removed too.
